Disgraced former Republican Congressman George Santos tried to defend President Trump's countless lies by explaining to host Bill Maher, but his argument was so far-fetched that it could become the new "alternative facts".

During an appearance on Maher's podcast "Club Random," Maher pointed out that the president "has told more lies than every other president combined," but Santos pushed back.

"I don't know if that's true," said Santos, who won his seat in Congress in 2022 with an almost entirely fabricated personal history.

Maher fired back immediately.

"You know that's true," Maher said passionately. "You know, even his supporters say, 'We take him seriously, not literally,'" he added, noting that Trump "says whatever pops into his head at any given moment."

Santos then tried to explain away Trump's constant dishonesty as something more than just habitual lying.

"Here's the question — is it a lie? Or is it a strategic... like a disruption of the matrix? I think — I'm not making excuses — but I just want to throw that out there for you," he said.

While "disruption of the matrix" sounds like the rightful successor to "alternative facts," the term former White House counselor Kellyanne Conway coined in January 2017 to explain away discrepancies with the Trump administration's reality, Maher was not buying it.

"Try using that logic in a relationship," Maher said, adding: "'Honey, I didn't sleep with that cocktail waitress, it's just a rupture in the matrix.'"

Santos tried to further clarify, but Maher cut him off, saying: "We are now redefining the word 'lie.'"
